numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On non-nanosecond data, round/floor/ceil silently rounded to the wrong granularity: Timedelta("6s").as_unit("s").round("2500ms") returned Timedelta('0 days 00:00:06') and Timedelta("4s").as_unit("s").ceil("2500ms") returned Timedelta('0 days 00:00:04'), a value that is not a multiple of the requested freq. The freq was silently truncated because get_unit_for_round converted it into the object's resolution with round_ok=True.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Nanosecond resolution gives 5s for the round example. A freq that is a whole multiple of the unit rounds normally; a freq that divides one unit evenly is a no-op; anything else raises ValueError with the message used in core/arrays/_ranges.py (freq=... is incompatible with unit=...).
trigger_conditions: object resolution is non-nanosecond (e.g. second resolution via as_unit("s"))
freq is not exactly representable in the object's resolution, e.g. freq="2500ms" on second-resolution data
operation is round, floor or ceil on Timestamp, DatetimeIndex, TimedeltaIndex or Series.dt, which all share the helper

input_output_examples.expected_output: a value that is a multiple of 2500ms (ValueError is raised for this freq under the fix)

oracle_clues: Nanosecond resolution gives 5s for the round example (pr_body reproducer comment)
Result must be a multiple of the requested freq for ceil
Non-divisor, non-multiple freqs now raise ValueError reusing the core/arrays/_ranges.py message

numerical_characteristics.precision: second resolution (unit 's') and microsecond/nanosecond units are used in the examples; the non-nano resolution is the target of the fix
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Timedelta('6s') at unit 's' with freq '2500ms' returned 6s instead of 5s; .ceil('2500ms') returned 4s
category_specific_evidence: Timedelta("6s").as_unit("s").round("2500ms") returned 6s instead of the expected 5s (nanosecond resolution gives 5s)
Timedelta("6s").as_unit("s").ceil("2500ms") returned 4s, which is not a multiple of the requested freq 2500ms
Pd.Timedelta("4s").as_unit("s").ceil("2500ms") returned Timedelta('0 days 00:00:04'), not a multiple of the requested freq
Violated property: result of round/floor/ceil must be a multiple of the requested freq (ceil/floor/round rounding to a granularity that was requested)
get_unit_for_round used round_ok=True, silently truncating freq into the object resolution, rounding to a different granularity than requested
Bug reproduces identically for Timestamp, DatetimeIndex, TimedeltaIndex and Series.dt since they share the helper
Fix: freq that is a whole multiple of one unit rounds normally; freq dividing one unit evenly is a no-op; otherwise ValueError 'freq=... is incompatible with unit=...'
Regression tests parametrize unit/freq pairs such as ('s','700ms'), ('s','2500ms'), ('ms','3us'), ('us','300ns') and expect ValueError
reproduction_risks: Expected values for the nanosecond-resolution comparison depend on the reference behaviour described in the commit message
Behavior of freq that divides one unit evenly (no-op) versus the old nanos == 0 guard differs, so a reproduction must distinguish these cases
Test values sit off the freq grid (e.g. 6.500000001s); on-grid values make the check a no-op
